title: Which shampoo size is the cheapest?
description: A sachet and three bottles of shampoo have different volumes and prices. The video finds the price of one millilitre for each size, compares them, and tests whether price is in proportion to volume. Keeko doubts this and thinks the biggest bottle must be cheapest.
teaching_notes: One idea: to compare prices fairly, divide each price by its volume, and a bigger pack does not always give the lower price. Watch for students who pick the largest bottle without working out each rate.

source: A sachet of 6 mL costs ₹2, a 180 mL bottle ₹154, a 340 mL bo
video_script.why: The child sees that the price of one millilitre settles which size is cheapest, and that the prices are not in proportion to the volumes.
video_script.substitution: Divide each price by its volume, compare the four results, and test the ratio of volumes with the ratio of prices.
video_script.anchor: a sachet and three bottles of shampoo of different sizes, from the book
video_script.wrong_answer: the large bottle is the cheapest
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko picks the largest bottle because a bigger pack should cost less for each millilitre, without working out the sachet.
video_script.payoff_line: The sachet is cheapest for each millilitre

final_answer.value: The sachet is cheapest per mL here (about ₹0.33), then the large bottle (₹0.54); price is not proportional to volume
final_answer.spoken: The sachet is cheapest for each millilitre, at about zero point three three rupees, then the large bottle at zero point five four rupees, and price is not in proportion to volume

never_show: the large bottle marked as the cheapest
maths_rules: small bottle: 154 ÷ 180 ≈ 0.86; medium bottle: 276 ÷ 340 ≈ 0.81; large bottle: 540 ÷ 1000 = 0.54
order from lowest: sachet 0.33, large 0.54, medium 0.81, small 0.86
volumes 6 : 180 = 1 : 30 but prices 2 : 154 = 1 : 77, so not proportional

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about shampoo.
<bookmark mark='sachet'/>A sachet of six millilitres costs two rupees.
<bookmark mark='small'/>A small bottle of one hundred eighty millilitres costs one hundred fifty four rupees.
<bookmark mark='medium'/>A medium bottle of three hundred forty millilitres costs two hundred seventy six rupees.
<bookmark mark='large'/>A large bottle of one thousand millilitres costs five hundred forty rupees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which size gives the cheapest shampoo for each millilitre?

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>If price and volume were in proportion, every size would cost the same for one millilitre.
<bookmark mark='fair'/>To compare fairly, we find the price of one millilitre for each size.
<bookmark mark='div'/>We get it by dividing the price by the volume.

narration: <bookmark mark='div'/>Step one, divide the price by the volume for each size.
<bookmark mark='sachet'/>The sachet gives two divided by six, which is about zero point three three rupees.
<bookmark mark='small'/>The small bottle gives one hundred fifty four divided by one hundred eighty, about zero point eight six.
<bookmark mark='medium'/>The medium bottle gives two hundred seventy six divided by three hundred forty, about zero point eight one.
<bookmark mark='large'/>The large bottle gives five hundred forty divided by one thousand, which is zero point five four.

beats.on_screen: order of the rates, lowest first: sachet 0.33, large 0.54, medium 0.81, small 0.86

narration: <bookmark mark='order'/>Step two, compare the four prices for one millilitre. The sachet is lowest. Then comes the large bottle, then the medium bottle, then the small bottle.

narration: <bookmark mark='vol'/>Step three, test the proportion. The volumes six and one hundred eighty are in the ratio one to thirty.
<bookmark mark='price'/>The prices two and one hundred fifty four are in the ratio one to seventy seven.
<bookmark mark='diff'/>The ratios differ, so the price is not in proportion to the volume.

beats.on_screen: Answer: The sachet is cheapest per mL here (about ₹0.33), then the large bottle (₹0.54); price is not proportional to volume

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the large bottle is the cheapest. A bigger pack should cost less for each millilitre.
<bookmark mark='sachet'/>But the sachet is the smallest pack, and its rate is lower than the large bottle.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A bigger pack does not always give a lower price, so we must work out every size.
<bookmark mark='waste'/>Remember too that many small sachets make much more plastic waste.
